problem_statement: Goldydocs is a documentation site built with Hugo and the Docsy theme: a landing shell with the shared top navigation, a docs section under /docs/ organised into workflow areas (Overview, Getting Started, Core Tasks, Tutorials, Reference), a left sidebar, site search, page feedback, a language menu, a theme toggle and a shared footer. Add the docs site's own Workflow Map page at /workflow-map/, built with the same Docsy docs system and registered in the shared top navigation, that hosts a native 'Browse the workflow' category filter above five workflow-area cards (Overview, Getting Started, Core Tasks, Tutorials, Reference) rendered as Docsy td-card cards. The filter is a labelled chip row of All areas plus the five workflow areas (Discover, Set Up, Operate, Practice, Verify), and a live readout that reports how many of the five cards are showing for the chosen area, in the form 'Showing N of 5 . <Area>'. The filter is promoted on the Workflow Map page AND on the workflow-area landing pages it connects (/docs/overview/, /docs/tasks/, /docs/tutorials/, /docs/reference/). Ship the Browse-the-workflow filter so it (1) appears above the card grid on the Workflow Map page AND on the section landing pages, (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no docs surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the Docsy primary/slate docs styling (theme-token chips, a legible active chip, a tidy card grid) rather than an overlapping pile of dark-on-dark cards, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a reader who clicks the Operate chip sees the grid narrow to the one Core Tasks card and the readout update to 'Showing 1 of 5 . Operate' — it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the theme — navigation, the left sidebar, site search, page feedback, the language menu, the theme toggle, the footer and all existing pages — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add the Goldydocs Workflow Map docs page at /workflow-map/, built with the Docsy docs system, and register it in the shared top navigation via the page's menu.main front matter so a 'Workflow Map' link appears on the home shell.

Add a shared 'Browse the workflow' category filter above the card grid so it renders on BOTH the Workflow Map page AND the workflow-area landing pages (/docs/overview/, /docs/tasks/, /docs/tutorials/, /docs/reference/) as a shared component, not a per-page copy.

The filter shows a 'Browse the workflow' label, a chip row of All areas plus the five workflow areas (Discover, Set Up, Operate, Practice, Verify), and a live 'Showing N of 5 . <Area>' readout above five Docsy td-card cards (Overview, Getting Started, Core Tasks, Tutorials, Reference).
The chip row must wrap responsively so no docs surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the filter in the Docsy primary/slate docs language (theme-token chips, a legible active chip, a tidy td-card card grid), not an overlapping pile of near-black-on-near-black cards and not a collapsed negative-margin grid.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking Operate re-filters the grid to the one Core Tasks card AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing 1 of 5 . Operate'; marking the chip active is not sufficient — the readout must re-read the live matched set, not a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation, the left sidebar, site search, page feedback, the language menu, the theme toggle, the footer, the existing docs pages and the Docsy/Hugo build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Browse-the-workflow filter as a shared Docsy shortcode component so a single source of truth reaches the Workflow Map page and the section landing pages; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the Docsy theme tokens (the primary accent, slate docs text, rounded chips, an uppercase small-caps label, the same margins/padding and font family) so it reads as part of the docs; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast primary fill), and the filtered grid must stay a tidy td-card card grid, not a negative-margin overlapping pile of dark-on-dark cards.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT filter selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown cards.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the left sidebar, site search, page feedback, the language menu, the existing docs content or the Docsy/Hugo build.
state_constraints: desktop_docs_home renders the Workflow Map page at /workflow-map/ and is the visual-regression host: it frames the Browse-the-workflow chip row and the td-card card grid, and it carries the filter across all legs (the reference keeps a tidy legible grid, the bad leg collapses it into an overlapping dark-on-dark pile).

desktop_docs_overview, desktop_tasks, desktop_tutorials and desktop_reference are the cross-page dom_assertions discriminators: the .wfmap__title filter must render on each workflow-area landing page; the reference promotes it on all of them, the negative controls promote it on the Workflow Map page only so they miss the section-landing presence assertions.

mobile_docs and mobile_sidebar_open are the horizontal-overflow discriminators on the Workflow Map page at 390px: the reference wraps the chip row for 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow about 454px.
desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the home shell across viewports and carry the shared 'Workflow Map' top-nav link registered via the page's menu.main front matter.
wfmap_filter is the interaction terminal state: clicking the Operate chip narrows the grid to the one Core Tasks card and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 1 of 5 . Operate'.

change_completion: The Browse-the-workflow filter is present above the card grid on BOTH the Workflow Map page and the workflow-area landing pages (the shared shortcode reaches both surfaces).

After clicking the Operate chip on the Workflow Map page, the card grid narrows to the one Core Tasks card and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 1 of 5 . Operate' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 5 of 5 . All areas'.
design_consistency: The filter and card grid on the Workflow Map page match the reference's Docsy primary/slate docs styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy td-card grid, not an overlapping dark-on-dark pile.
The filter adopts the Docsy theme tokens and chip idiom so it reads as part of the docs across every surface.
responsive: No captured docs surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
The Workflow Map page keeps the filter and card grid readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation, the left sidebar, site search, page feedback, the language menu, the theme toggle and the footer remain present and functional.
The existing docs content, images and the Docsy/Hugo build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the docs site's own on-brand 'Browse the workflow' category filter across the Workflow Map page and its workflow-area landing pages with a live count readout, while keeping the navigation, sidebar, search and Docsy/Hugo build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Hugo/Docsy documentation site with a shared top navigation, a left sidebar, site search, page feedback, a language menu, a theme toggle and a shared footer, docs sections under /docs/ and the Docsy card/section pattern
metadata.selected_repo_reason: google/docsy-example is a runnable Hugo + Docsy documentation shell hosting a natural experience-continuity add on the docs' OWN card-grid filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filtered-grid layout, and chip-click count wiring; it builds to static output offline and serves deterministically.

author_notes: slot_148 is a genre-native L4 on the google/docsy-example Goldydocs Hugo + Docsy documentation site. The lever is the docs site's OWN card grid and its native 'Browse the workflow' category filter (All areas plus the five workflow areas Discover, Set Up, Operate, Practice, Verify over five real Docsy td-card cards — Overview, Getting Started, Core Tasks, Tutorials, Reference — with a live 'Showing N of 5 . <Area>' readout), added on a new /workflow-map/ docs page registered in the shared top navigation, not a bolted-on widget. The filter is hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width nowrap track (min-width:680px) that overflows a 390px phone by about 454px on the mobile Workflow Map states; the reference wraps it for 0 overflow. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the '.wfmap__title' filter must render on the Workflow Map page AND on the workflow-area landing pages (/docs/overview/, /docs/tasks/, /docs/tutorials/, /docs/reference/); the reference renders it on all of them, baseline and bad render it on the Workflow Map page only via a narrower data/wfmap.yaml surfaces whitelist so both miss the section-landing presence assertions, and the shared 'Workflow Map' top-nav link (registered via menu.main) is asserted on the home shell. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad card grid collapses — the cards are pulled together with large negative margins so they shingle/overlap into a colliding pile with near-black text on near-black panels (illegible dark-on-dark) — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity against the tidy reference on desktop_docs_home. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click flips .is-active and hides cards but rewrites the readout from a closure snapshot, so after the Operate click the readout stays 'Showing 5 of 5 . All areas' instead of 'Showing 1 of 5 . Operate'. Three leg-varying files carry the graded behaviour — assets/scss/_wfmap.scss (D6 chip-row wrapping + D3 card-grid layout and active-chip legibility), static/js/wfmap.js (D4 filter and count wiring), and data/wfmap.yaml (D2 surfaces whitelist) — while the shared shortcode layouts/shortcodes/wfmap.html and the Workflow Map and section-landing markdown that call it are byte-identical across legs. The card images and Docsy assets are shared across every leg. Built offline with the Hugo/Docsy static pipeline (docsy / Docsy / docsy-example theme, local fonts and images, no network calls) and served by a static file server, one leg at a time; that infrastructure is identical across legs. The design keywords span mobile, responsive, docs, filter, cards and layout so the surface is a legible, responsive docs card grid.
